title: Relearning to Trust My Knee After Surgery
script: Narrator: [reflective] Six weeks after the surgeon reconstructed my torn ligament, I still flinched every time I stepped off a curb, half convinced the knee would give way beneath me.

Narrator: [honest] The physiotherapist kept insisting that the joint was structurally sound again, yet no amount of reassurance could override the memory of that first, sickening pop on the football pitch.
Narrator: [frustrated] What nobody had warned me about was how tedious recovery would be, how much of it consisted of small, unglamorous exercises repeated until they became almost meaningless.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I had always assumed healing was something that simply happened to you, passively, while you waited it out on the sofa with your leg elevated.
Narrator: [surprised] Instead, I discovered that recovery demanded a kind of discipline I had never needed for the sport itself, since motivation is easy when you are winning.
Narrator: [determined] Three sets of quad exercises before breakfast, ice afterward, a resistance band looped around the doorframe each evening, whether or not I felt like bothering.
Narrator: [honest] There were days I resented the whole process, particularly when a teammate posted videos of himself training as though nothing in the world could touch him.
Narrator: [grateful] My physiotherapist, a patient man named Yusuf, eventually told me to stop measuring my recovery against anyone else's timeline, since no two ligaments heal identically.
Narrator: [thoughtful] That advice sounds obvious written down, but hearing it from someone who had watched hundreds of knees heal carried a weight my own reasoning never managed.
Narrator: [hopeful] By the fourth month, I could finally jog in a straight line without that instinctive hesitation, though sharp turns still made me noticeably nervous.
Narrator: [reflective] I used to think confidence returned the moment the injury healed, but I now understand that the body trusts itself only after evidence, not after permission.
Narrator: [warmly] These days, when the knee twinges after a long run, I no longer panic; I simply rest it, the way Yusuf taught me, and wait.
Narrator: [peacefully] Recovery, I learned, is less a return to who you were and more a slow negotiation with who your body has quietly become.

quiz.question: How did the narrator react to ordinary movements weeks after her surgery?
options: She avoided leaving the house entirely
She flinched, half convinced the knee would give way
She felt no lingering fear at all
She stopped attending physiotherapy
quiz.explanation: She says she still flinched stepping off a curb, half convinced the knee would give way beneath her.

quiz.question: What did the narrator not expect about recovery?
options: That it would be quick
How tedious it would be, full of small repeated exercises
That it required no effort
That it would be painless
quiz.explanation: She says nobody warned her how tedious recovery would be, consisting of small, unglamorous exercises.

quiz.question: What made her feel further behind in her recovery?
options: Her physiotherapist's schedule
Comparing herself to a teammate's effortless training videos
A second injury
Missing appointments
quiz.explanation: She resented the process particularly when a teammate posted videos of himself training effortlessly.

quiz.question: What did Yusuf, her physiotherapist, eventually tell her?
options: To quit the sport
To stop measuring her recovery against anyone else's timeline
To ice her knee only once a week
To skip her exercises
quiz.explanation: Yusuf told her to stop comparing her recovery to others, since no two ligaments heal identically.

quiz.question: What conclusion does the narrator reach about confidence and healing?
options: Confidence returns the instant an injury heals
The body trusts itself only after evidence, not permission
Confidence has nothing to do with physical recovery
She never regained confidence in her knee
quiz.explanation: She concludes the body trusts itself only after evidence, not after permission.
